prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: Yale Symphony Orchestra, records (RU 1210). Manuscripts and Archives, Yale University Library.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Yale Symphony Orchestra was founded in 1965 and performed as the Calhoun Chamber Orchestra, Yale Symphonic Society, and Yale Symphonic Orchestra before adopting its current name by 1968. Since its inception, the orchestra consists of current Yale students and is conducted by Yale faculty or graduate students. The orchestra performs several times each year in Woolsey Hall and over live-stream to an audience of several thousand spectators and, since 1971, has periodically gone on performance tours in Europe, South America, and Asia. Performances include a wide range of music, including traditional Western European classical music, American heritage, and American contemporary music. Information for this historical note was taken from the Yale Symphony Orchestra website, "The Fifty-Year Crescendo" by Teresa Chen in the Yale Daily News, "Making music for a half century" by Christopher Arnott in the Yale Alumni Magazine, and the contents of Series 2027-A-0001: Digital posters, programs, and photographs.

odd.head: General
odd.p: Forms part of Record Group 40 (YRG 40), Records of Yale Clubs, Societies, and Organizations

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: The collection is open for research. Items from this collection may be requested by contacting Yale Special Collections at beinecke.library@yale.edu.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection consists of photographs and posters documenting the history of the Yale Symphony Orchestra.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged chronologically by a conductor's directorship.
